# Isotopic composition and fractionation {#sec-isotopic-composition-and-fractionation}

The carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) flows and pool tracked in the model are comprising all major
isotopes (i.e. C = $\mathrm{^{12}C}$ + $\mathrm{^{13}C}$ + $\mathrm{^{14}C}$, and N =
$\mathrm{^{14}N}$ + $\mathrm{^{15}N}$). The model explicitly tracks the mass flow of
$\mathrm{^{13}C}$, $\mathrm{^{14}C}$ and $\mathrm{^{15}N}$ as separate entities for all
biogeochemical pools and fluxes. The molar mixing ratio ($R_X$) of the isotope (e.g.
$\mathrm{^{13}C)}$ to the main element (e.g. $\mathrm{^{12}C}$) of each biogeochemical pool can be
calculated as

$$
R_{13C} = \frac{^{13}C}{^{12}C} = \frac{^{13}C}{C - ^{13}C}
$$

####{#eq-iso-ratio}

and by convention

$$
\label{eq-isotope-delta-notation}
\delta_{13C} = ( \frac{R_{13C}}{ R_{ref,13C}} - 1 ) \times 1000
$$

##{#eq-isotope-delta-notation}

where $R_{ref,13C}$ is the reference isotopic molar mixing ratio. Similar
calculations are done for the ratio of $\mathrm{^{15}N}$ to $\mathrm{^{14}N}$ and the reference
value $R_{ref,15N}$. By convention, the delta notation of $\mathrm{^{14}C}$ is dependent on the
$\mathrm{^{13}C}$ content, see @Levin:2010fu, and the molar mass of $\mathrm{^{14}C}$ is ignored
in the calculations of $\mathrm{^{13}C}$ because of the extremely low concentrations.

Biogeochemical processes discriminate against the heavier isotope, and this fractionation process is
treated by calculating the mixing ratio of the isotope of the resulting flux as

$$
\label{eq-isotope-fractionation}
R_{sink} = \frac{R_{source}}{\frac{\epsilon_{process}}{1000}+1}
$$

##%{#eq-isotope-fractionation}

where $R_{source}$ is the molar mixing ratio of the source pool of the reaction, $R_{sink}$ is the
molar mixing ratio of the resulting matter flux, and $\epsilon_{process}$ is a process- and isotope-specific discrimination rate.

Isotopic discrimination of $\mathrm{^{13}C}$ and $\mathrm{^{14}C}$ by photosynthesis is modelled
according to the general equation derived by @Farquhar:1982ks; @Drake:2014dl, so that

$$
\label{eq-ps-discrimination}
D_x = a_x + ( c_x + \phi_{C4} \times b_x - a_x )  \frac{c_i}{c_a}
$$

where $a_x$, and $b_x$ are isotope-specific constants ($\mathrm{^{13}C}$ and $\mathrm{^{14}C}$,
respectively, see @tbl-isotope:param). $c_x$ and $\phi_{C4}$ account for the additional bundle-sheath
processes in C4 plants. For C3 plants, these processes do not play a role and these parameters are 0
and 1, respectively. In the model, currently only photosynthesis is assumed to result in C-isotope
discrimination, ignoring the effect of the smaller and uncertain discrimination by tissue
construction, storage formation and respiration [@Bruggemann:2011co].

Isotopic discrimination for various nitrogen cycle processes (e.g. biological nitrogen fixation,
ammonification, plant and microbial N uptake, and processes associated with nitrification and
denitrification) are taken from @Robinson2001-hy. According to @Robinson2001-hy, in case of
near-complete consumption of the source pool, the discrimination is reduced as

$$
\epsilon_{process}^{corr} = \epsilon_{process} (f_{source}-1)log(\frac{1-f_{source}}{f_{source}})
$$

where $f_{source}$ is the ratio of the source consumption to the source pool size.
